key_insight: Halide ordering, not just composition, strongly controls miscibility and structural phase transitions in mixed-halide perovskites, shifting transition temperatures by up to 100 K.
engineering_relevance: For solar-cell materials design, tuning halide and A-site composition can improve phase stability and help avoid temperature-driven instabilities in device operation.
method: Trained machine-learned interatomic potentials on DFT reference data for CsxRb1-xPbBr3yI3-3y, CsxRb1-xPbBr3yCl3-3y, and CsxRb1-xPbCl3yI3-3y.
Used large-scale hybrid Monte Carlo–molecular dynamics simulations to sample both configurational and vibrational degrees of freedom.
Mapped miscibility gaps and temperature-dependent halide ordering across compositions and linked them to structural phase boundaries.
evidence_signal: The simulations show miscibility gaps in all three binary systems, with Br-Cl and Br-I closing at low temperatures, Cl-I persisting above room temperature, and experimentally relevant non-linear phase-boundary behavior reproduced in CsPbBr3yI3-3y.
watch_item: The conclusions rely on MLIP fidelity to DFT and may need experimental validation for specific processing conditions, defects, and device-scale microstructures.
paper_title: Strong Impact of Halide Ordering on Structural Phase Transitions in Mixed Perovskites
